### How to use
1. At first, you should [install the F-Droid app](https://f-droid.org/), it's an alternative app store for Android.
2. Now you can copy the following [link](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Foxu89/fdroid-cloudstream/main/fdroid/repo?fingerprint=ABA20153B521090F8888A2570A27256F57840F6C2F2F1B8EFE8EA5CCC208A975), then add this repository to your F-Droid client:

    ```
    https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Foxu89/fdroid-cloudstream/main/fdroid/repo?fingerprint=ABA20153B521090F8888A2570A27256F57840F6C2F2F1B8EFE8EA5CCC208A975
    ```

    Alternatively, you can also scan this QR code:

    <p align="center">
      <img src=".github/qrcode.png?raw=true" alt="F-Droid repo QR code"/>
    </p>

3. Open the link in F-Droid. It will ask you to add the repository. Everything should already be filled in correctly, so just press "OK".
4. You can now install CloudStream (stable or pre-release) from the F-Droid client.

Please note that some apps published here might contain [Anti-Features](https://f-droid.org/en/docs/Anti-Features/). If you can't find an app by searching for it, you can go to settings and enable "Include anti-feature apps".

### For developers
If you are a developer and want to publish your own apps right from GitHub Actions as an F-Droid repo, you can fork/copy this repo and see  [the documentation](setup.md) for more information on how to set it up.

### [License](LICENSE)
The license is for the files in this repository, *except* those in the `fdroid` directory. These files *might* be licensed differently; you can use an F-Droid client to get the details for each app.
